yui.title: Almost Coffee
yui.text:
Yui finds you on the back steps at dusk with two cups of something that is almost coffee. She has been working on it for a week. It smells of burnt barley.

You each take a sip, and you pull exactly the same face.

After that the two of you talk about home, for hours. Train transfers, and which line you each took. The convenience store that stayed open all night. The vending machine on the fourth floor, outside Accounting, that ate her coins and nobody else's.

She remembers things about you that you'd forgotten. You brought the stapler back every time. You always held the lift.

"I used to practice saying good morning to you," she says to her cup. "In the lift, on the way up. Then the doors would open, and I'd say it to the whole office so it wouldn't mean anything."

She pushes her glasses up, twice. Then she takes them off and wipes her eyes with her sleeve.

You find that you're doing the same.
ngpp: Even talking about Tokyo's fourth-floor vending machine feels normal—until Yui pauses blinking sideways at the courtyard lantern post, whispering that the shadow across the steps gave her sudden déjà vu.
"I remember every awful office instant coffee back home," Yui murmurs softly, clutching her mug tight. "So why did my hands reach straight for your favorite chipped mug without even asking, Sam?"

"My mind stops right at the Tokyo crosswalk, Takahashi-kun," Yui whispers, setting her mug neatly beside your knee as if she's sat on these steps a hundred times. "Yet every bone in my shoulders knows you like two spoons of sugar in Hollowmere too."

choices.label: Sit with her until the cups go cold
choices.res: You stay there together until the cups are cold and the lanterns are lit, shoulders touching, saying the names of train stations like prayers. She files the evening under "keep."

choices.label: Pass her a napkin and a joke
choices.res: You offer a napkin and a terrible vending machine joke. {N} laughs wetly, pushes up her glasses, and leans just a little against the step rail closer to you.

image.comp: sitting on back steps with him holding two steaming cups, laughing about home
image.setting: back steps of an inn at night, lanterns, stars

yui.title: Bath Time Budget Meeting
yui.text:
You're in the tub when the washroom door opens and Yui walks straight in. She's looking for the ledger. She is saying so as she comes, and she's four steps into the room before the steam rolls over her glasses and fogs them white.

She stops.

She doesn't leave. You get the sense that leaving would mean admitting something has happened.

She stares at the ceiling. Then she stares at the floor, and then at the ceiling again. She has the account book clutched against her chest like a shield, and her ears have gone the color of boiled shrimp.

"The linen totals," she says faintly. "I thought they might be in here. They obviously aren't." She still can't see anything through her glasses, and she doesn't take them off. "I'm going to stand here for a moment, Takahashi-san. Sam. I'm so sorry. I've forgotten where the door is."

1.title: Off the Ledger
1.text:
Yui knocks before she comes in this time. She has a stack of folded towels, and her glasses fog over the instant she sees you sitting waist-deep in the tub.

She doesn't drop the towels, and she doesn't start reciting numbers. She swallows. Then she takes off her cardigan, folds it, rolls her blouse sleeves to the elbow, and kneels down beside the wooden rim with her cheeks on fire.

"You've been at the ledgers until midnight all week, Sam. I've watched you rub your neck." She picks up the cloth and the soap. "Let me wash your shoulders, at least. I'd like to. I've wanted to do something for you for about six years."

choices.label: Let her wash your back—then pull her close for a slow kiss
choices.res: Yui's small, warm hands tremble lightly as soapy lather glides down your collarbones—and when you lean up to catch her damp lips through the steam, she makes a soft, helpless sound and lets the towel fall.
choices.fallbackRes: Her small soap-slick hands tremble against your shoulders for two heartbeats before settling into slow, careful circles while she leans her flushed forehead gently against your neck.

choices.label: Thank her gently and save her glasses from the steam
choices.res: She exhales a shaky little laugh, wiping her lenses on her apron while promising not to log "one soaked cardigan" under operating losses.

image.comp: kneeling beside the wooden rim with cloth and soap, glasses fogged, cardigan folded aside, bright red cheeks, shy earnest look
image.wear: a blouse with the sleeves rolled to the elbows

3.title: Closing Entries
3.text:
Steam curls out past you when you push the washroom door open.

Yui is already in the cedar tub. Her glasses are folded on top of a towel, and her dark hair is pinned up off the back of her neck. She's naked, and the water only comes to just below her tits. For once she isn't holding anything in front of herself, not a book or a towel.

She looks at you, a little blurred without the glasses, and lifts both wet hands out of the water.

"No audit tonight, Sam." Her voice only shakes slightly. "Bolt the door and get in with me. I've done the figures on how long I've waited, and I'm not waiting any longer."

choices.label: Lock the bolt and slip into the hot water with her
choices.res: Yui climbs straight into your lap the moment warm water closes over your waist, clinging tightly around your shoulders as she gasps your name in quiet, unguarded bliss beneath the mist.

choices.label: Wash her slowly from collarbone to thighs
choices.res: She leans softly back against your bare chest, shivering beneath every slow pass of your soapy hands until her hips press insistently back against yours.

image.comp: sitting in the cedar tub with dark hair pinned up, glasses off, both wet hands lifted out of the water, blurry-eyed brave look, nothing held in front of her

choices.label: "Could you pass me a towel?"
choices.res: She throws it directly at your face and flees, the account book forgotten on the stool. You find a neat sticky note inside: "Variance: 1 towel."

choices.label: Act completely casual
choices.res: She stammers through the entire weekly budget review, right there, without once looking down, glasses fogged, voice cracking on "depreciation." It's honestly impressive. You approve every line item.

choices.label: Yell
choices.res: She flees, mortified, glasses clattering on the tiles, and avoids you for three days, sliding reports under your door instead of speaking.

image.comp: standing in a washroom doorway clutching a ledger, staring fixedly at the ceiling, bright red
image.setting: steamy wooden washroom, a man in the tub off-frame

yui.title: Instant Ramen, Reconstructed
yui.text:
Yui has a secret, and tonight she shows you. For a month she has been trying to recreate instant ramen in the house kitchen.

She has notes. There are fourteen pages of them, with columns.

The broth is a pale, apologetic grey. The noodles have the texture of wet rope. There's something floating in it that she says is meant to be the little dried vegetables.

It's terrible. You eat all of it anyway. You pass the one chipped bowl back and forth across the kitchen table, and she watches every mouthful go in.

"Do you remember covering my Friday shift?" she asks. Her eyes are fixed on the steam. "The weekend it rained. My mother was ill and I hadn't told anyone. You just said, 'I've got it, go.' You didn't ask why."

She turns the bowl a quarter of the way round.

"I liked you a long time before the truck, Sam. I had it filed under 'later'. I thought there'd be a later."

choices.label: Step around the table and kiss six years of waiting right off her lips
choices.res: You push the terrible bowls aside and cup her burning cheeks in both hands; Yui drops her chopsticks at once and pulls you close, glasses bumping your nose as six years of quiet office yearning finally spills loose.

choices.label: Tell her you liked her too, then finish the bowl
choices.res: You tell her, a little clumsily, and she covers her face with the cup. You scrape the bowl clean together. She says it's the best ramen she's ever made, and for once she is not lying about it.

choices.label: Declare it a triumph of accounting
choices.res: "Best ramen in the realm," you say, which is technically true. {N} laughs, tucks her hair behind her ear, and doesn't take back what she said.

image.comp: eating a terrible bowl of homemade ramen with him at a kitchen table, both laughing
image.setting: small inn kitchen at night, pots and steam

yui.title: The Way Home
yui.text:
A travelling mage has set up in the market square. His flyers say that he can open the way home for otherworlders. He'll send them back to where they came from, for a fee.

Yui brings you one. Her hands are shaking, and the ink has smeared where she has been holding it too long. It smells of cheap incense.

She stands in the office doorway and won't come in.

"It's probably a fraud. I looked at his arithmetic and it doesn't balance." She's talking too fast. "But I keep thinking about my mother, and my desk, and the plant on it that nobody will have watered."

She looks down at the flyer.

"Nobody waited up for either of us back there. I know that. I used to leave the office at ten and the only light on in my building was the vending machine." Her voice goes very small. "But if it were real. Would you go?"
ngpp: Folding the flyer along crisp office creases, she blinks sideways at the desk as if wondering why giving up Hollowmere pinched harder than leaving Tokyo.
"Wait—why does leaving THIS office hurt almost as much as Tokyo did, Sam?" Yui whispers, fingers whitening on the doorframe.

Yui drops the flyer straight onto the lamp tray before finishing the question. "Honestly, Sam—I remember every Tokyo apartment block by heart, and somehow every cycle I still choose sitting right across from you here."

choices.label: "I'd stay. This is home now."
choices.res: She lets out a breath she's been holding for a week, shoulders dropping an inch, and straightens the flyer into a neat square before putting it away.

choices.label: "I don't know."
choices.res: Honest. It still hurts. She nods, pushes her glasses up, and files the flyer in a drawer. She doesn't bring it up again.

choices.label: "Only if you came with me."
choices.res: She laughs and wipes her eyes under her glasses. (The mage turns out to be a fraud. Neither of you is disappointed.)

image.comp: holding a crumpled flyer with shaking hands, looking up at him with teary eyes

yui.title: Festival Night
yui.text:
Yui takes hold of your cuff and pulls you into Hollowmere's harvest festival. There are lanterns strung across the square, and fried honey dough, and barkers shouting. Cider is being warmed over pine embers.

She has a list of the stalls. She has put them in order.

At the ring toss she studies the spinning bottle for a full minute, with her lips moving. She's working out the rotation. Then she lands three brass rings in a row and wins the largest prize on the rack.

It's a stuffed wyvern. It's badly made, with a crooked neck and two button eyes that don't match.

She insists that you carry it. You carry it under one arm all evening. She walks beside you giggling into her collar, because the town guards have decided it's a mascot and keep saluting it.

"We never did anything like this," she says, quite happily. "Six years, and we never once went anywhere. I'm making up the difference."

2.text:
Yui pulls you through the lantern-strung festival holding your elbow, and not your sleeve. Her cheeks are bright pink from the spiced cider and the heat of the crowd.

She wins the crooked stuffed wyvern at the ring toss and makes you carry it. Then, in the middle of the square, she takes your free hand and tucks it into her coat pocket with hers, where nobody can see.

Her fingers lace through yours in the dark of the pocket and squeeze.

"The lantern parade is at nine," she says, close to your ear. "It's the best part. I had it on the list." Her thumb strokes the inside of your wrist. "I don't feel like sharing you with a parade. Could we go home early?"

image.comp: walking close with her hand tucked in a coat pocket laced with his, whispering at his ear, cheeks pink from cider, holding a crooked stuffed wyvern

choices.label: Wear it like a hat, proudly
choices.res: Yui laughs so hard she has to sit down on an ale keg while strangers cheer your awful posture and crooked spectacles gleam beneath paper lanterns.

choices.label: Win her one back
choices.res: It takes eleven tries, half a silver pouch, and clear pity from the stallkeeper—yet her slightly-less-ugly griffin keeps guard right beside her stapler forever.

choices.label: Slip home early before the lantern parade ends
choices.res: Yui tucks the stuffed wyvern neatly onto the entryway shelf, latches your bedroom door, and pushes her glasses straight onto the table before kissing you breathlessly.

image.comp: at a harvest festival handing him an ugly stuffed wyvern prize, triumphant grin
image.setting: harvest festival at night, game stalls, paper lanterns

yui.title: Second Chance
yui.text:
At the weekly staff meeting, Yui sits down next to you and takes your hand under the table.

She doesn't let go of it. She reads out the quarterly figures in a perfectly level voice, turning the pages with her other hand. All the while her thumb is tracing slow circles on the inside of your wrist. Nobody notices. You don't hear a single number.

Afterward the two of you are alone in the office. The lamp is low, and the ledgers she has put in order are stacked up behind her.

"I've been thinking about what I'd have said, if I'd ever been brave enough in that lift." She takes off her glasses, looks at them, and puts them back on. "It was going to be 'Good morning, Takahashi-san. Would you like to get dinner?' It took me six years and I never said it."

She steps in close.

"This is a second life, and I'm not spending it being shy, Sam."

She kisses you. Her glasses bump your nose. Then she takes your hand again and pulls you toward her room.
ngpp: Her thumb traces that exact spot on your wrist as though she already learned how smoothly it steadies her voice.
"Tokyo never gave us overtime to stay together, Sam," she breathes softly outside her room, "yet why does closing this latch feel like a habit we've kept across worlds?"
"No goddess gets to file our second chance under 'closed,' Sam," Yui whispers fiercely against your collarbone as the bedroom door shuts. "I didn't cross worlds twice just to wait another night."
yui.goLead: Yui sets her glasses down beside the bedside lantern. She pulls you down to her by the strings of your hoodie and presses herself against your chest, flushed and trembling.

choices.label: Say yes
Not yet
choices.res: {N} nods and squeezes your hand once. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She pushes up her glasses and goes back to her columns, smiling.
